gap.x86_64: bioconda's x86 bioconductor-preprocesscore 1.72.0 (r45h01b2380_0) fails inside SeSAMe's normalisation with 'return code from pthread_create() is 22' on Intel (AVX-512, AMX), AMD Zen 5 and AMD Zen 3 (no AVX-512) alike, before any assertion. Measured cause (2026-10-21) - preprocessCore gives each thread a fixed PTHREAD_STACK_MIN + one page (qnorm.c:530), 20,480 bytes on x86_64, and the image's libopenblasp-r0.3.30 carries 143,360 bytes of static TLS, so glibc 2.36 refuses the stack; on arm64 PTHREAD_STACK_MIN is 131,072 and OpenBLAS 0.3.34's TLS is 61,440, so it fits. No environment variable sets that stack (the source reads only R_THREADS, a thread count), and R_THREADS=1 or 4, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 and GLIBC_TUNABLES nns=1/optional_static_tls=0 all still fail; the fix is a build with --disable-threading (bioconda/bioconda-recipes#31420). minfi's task passes on x86 (checked 2026-10-13)

traps.cause: the recipe's timed command pipes the SAM through `gzip -1`, and on x86 that times BusyBox's gzip, not bwa-mem2
traps.fix: keep compression off the timed path; put `samtools` or a multithreaded compressor behind it in production
traps.symptom: The recipe's AMD run took 1,114 s for `SRR062634`, with bwa-mem2 reporting 337 s of compute

traps.cause: package version != binary version
traps.fix: record the binary's own version (tool_version 2.2.1)
traps.symptom: `bwa-mem2 version` prints **2.2.1** from the package bioconda and aarch.bio both call 2.3

traps.cause: the integrator carries T and Y, not u, so u drifts by the per-step error summed over steps; a flat bound picked before any run ignores step count
traps.fix: bound u/h drift at rtol × CVODES steps per trajectory; re-run all three chips on the changed spec
traps.symptom: first run failed on Intel: internal-energy drift 1.66e-8 against a flat 1e-8 bound, on the 40 atm φ = 1 reactor at 1250 K (3,838 steps)

traps.cause: `copy.deepcopy` of an `iotbx.pdb` hierarchy round-trips through PDB format whenever the model fits it, rounding coordinates to 0.001 Å, B to 0.01 and U to 1e-4; `mmtbx.model.manager(model_input=...)` returns a hierarchy at PDB precision
traps.cost: moves F_calc by up to 2e-4 relative on this cohort
traps.fix: assert the scored structure equals the file's own atoms (as real.py does); a script that builds its own model manager computes on rounded atoms
traps.symptom: On `8abo`, 3.18593 became 3.186

traps.cause: CDO 2.6.1 computes the grid's cell areas again for every timestep when fldmean has to derive them
traps.cost: about 29 minutes per job over the year
traps.fix: -setgridarea,area.nc from one cdo gridarea (0.2 s); same mean within 5.4e-14
traps.symptom: cdo fldmean with no cell areas given: 148.0 s on January (Graviton4), 0.19 s per hour

traps.cause: the files store 27 × 139 × 277 chunks; NCO reads one hour at a time, so each hour decompresses its 27-hour slab again
traps.fix: --cnk_csh=1000000000 (1 GB cache); result bit-identical, ~12 s per file
traps.symptom: ncra with the default chunk cache: 277.4 s on January (Graviton4)

traps.blames: a decode overflow, which reads like a calendar or range problem
traps.cause: the time bytes are float64 but .zarray says int64; read as labelled they overflow
traps.fix: none applied; the refusal is correct and asserted (refusals-justified)
traps.symptom: cftime and xarray both refuse (OverflowError) on 236 stores (IPSL-CM6A-LR, CNRM-CM6-1, CNRM-ESM2-1)

traps.cause: the axes are stored out of order (first value 2101, last 2100); both ends fit datetime64[ns], so xarray takes the fast path and the values past 2262 overflow
traps.fix: decode with use_cftime=True, which decodes all 1,395 correctly
traps.symptom: no warning: the 465 values after 2262 in each axis decode to 1677–1715 (off by 2⁶⁴ ns, 584.5 years)

traps.cause: the floor was set before any run from a guess at Clair3's published HiFi numbers; all 432 FP and 315 of 318 FN indels lie in AllTandemRepeatsandHomopolymers_slop5
traps.fix: guard indel F1 in GIAB's easy stratum (1.00000) and report the all-region number
traps.symptom: indel F1 0.96682 failed the all-region floor of 0.98 on every chip

traps.cause: hap.py is linux-64 only on bioconda; rtg-tools 3.13 is noarch but aarch.bio has not built it
traps.fix: run RTG.jar extracted from bioconda's rtg-tools-3.13-hdfd78af_0.tar.bz2 under recipes/picard's pinned JVM
traps.symptom: No arm64 image of RTG Tools or hap.py exists

traps.cause: the files store 27-hour HDF5 chunks; a chunk split across two dask tasks is decompressed twice
traps.fix: align dask chunks to the file's chunks where the computation allows (the day x hour reshape here needs 24-hour chunks)
traps.symptom: pass 1 took 239 s with 24-hour dask chunks vs 132 s with 54-hour chunks

traps.cause: X.groupby("time.hour") - clim then .groupby("time.hour").mean() without flox (absent from the climate env): each hour group is a strided slice through every chunk
traps.cost: two OOM-killed runs
traps.fix: reshape the hourly axis: X.coarsen(time=24).construct(time=("day", "hour")) gives the identical climatology and streams at a 31 GiB peak
traps.symptom: OOM-killed at 64 GiB, twice, 7–70 s into the pass

traps.cause: posteriordb 1.1.0 is not uniform
traps.cost: found by two Graviton4 sizing runs
traps.fix: read both forms (real.py does)
traps.symptom: 11 of the 57 reference info files spell the diagnostics key `diagnostics_information` and 46 spell it `diagnostic_information`; one-parameter posteriors (`Rate_1`, `Rate_3`, `Rate_5`) store names and ESS as scalars, not one-element lists

traps.cause: its pattern `ENERGY\| Total FORCE_EVAL.+?:` needs a colon; the 2026.2 line `ENERGY| Total FORCE_EVAL ( QS ) energy [hartree]` has none
traps.fix: same criterion with a pattern that takes the number after the unit (real.py)
traps.symptom: upstream's check-release-comparison.py matches nothing on 2026.2 output

traps.cause: Cromwell's local backend starts each task as a sibling container through the host's Docker socket

traps.symptom: spawn's container path does not expose the socket

traps.cause: Intel's GKL PairHMM is x86-only; on Graviton every shard runs Java's `LOGLESS_CACHING` on one thread, and repeat-rich active regions hit it hardest
traps.fix: Split that region more finely if you run this on Graviton
traps.symptom: Shard 7 covers chr20:29–33 Mb, the pericentromere. It takes 4,999 s, while the other fifteen take 172–1,621 s. For the last 56 minutes, 15 of 16 cores sit idle.

traps.cause: Canvas.points labels the aggregate's dims with the input column names
traps.cost: found by a 2-file probe (two probes, $0.03)

traps.symptom: datashader names a raster's dims after its columns ('plat', 'plon'), not x/y

traps.cause: datashader's sum reduction leaves cells with no points as NaN
traps.cost: found by a 2-file probe (two probes, $0.03)
traps.fix: assert sum and mean are NaN exactly where the count is 0 (now an in-task assertion)
traps.symptom: its `sum` is NaN, not 0, in an empty cell

traps.cause: at bin width W bamCoverage credits a read to every bin it touches, spreading it over ~L-1+W positions; the metric compared a binned quantity with an unbinned one
traps.fix: --binSize 1, where L-1+W = L and the identity holds by construction
traps.symptom: integral vs samtools mapped bases at --binSize 50, within 5%: measured 1.644889 — refused

traps.cause: samtools 'bases mapped (cigar)' counts M and I; reference coverage counts M only
traps.fix: subtract the inserted bases summed from samtools stats ID lines (exactly 132,420) — accounting, not tolerance
traps.symptom: at binSize 1 the integral came out 4.4e-05 short — 132,420 bases in 3.0 Gbp

traps.cause: the packaged module carries no __version__
traps.fix: getattr fallback reporting 'unknown'; take the version from bamCoverage --version
traps.symptom: deeptools.__version__ is absent in this build

traps.cause: BusyBox awk in the x86 (bioconda) image
traps.cost: about $0.9 for three runs stopped at their check glue
traps.fix: search.sh hashes the 20k clusters instead of the 38.8M ids
traps.symptom: check glue hashing 38.8M ids would have taken hours on the x86 image's BusyBox awk

traps.cause: UniRef leaves out sequences shorter than 11 residues; the 8 unmapped queries are exactly those
traps.cost: $1.79 (the first Graviton4 run)

traps.symptom: FAIL: only 20423 of 20431 queries map to a UniRef50 cluster

traps.cause: the API serialises the bucket's integral floats as integers (proj:transform 20.0 -> 20)
traps.fix: compare value for value, or API to API / bucket to bucket, never across by hash
traps.symptom: every API item differs from its bucket file when compared as raw JSON (18,346 of 18,346)

traps.cause: Earth Search builds its next-page token from each item's datetime; excluding properties gives a good first page and page 2 fails server-side
traps.fix: `fields` must keep `properties.datetime`
traps.symptom: parse_exception: cannot parse empty date

traps.blames: the server, generically; the error does not say "page too big"
traps.cause: a page cannot be larger than ~6 MB: limit=1000 full items fails; limit=260 (5.57 MB) returns 200, limit=300 returns 502
traps.fix: keep full-item searches at pystac-client's default of 100; ids-only searches page fine at 1000
traps.symptom: APIError: {"message": "Internal server error"}

traps.cause: aarch.science's hep env ships no h5py/HDF5 Python reader, and the Zenodo record is HDF5
traps.fix: convert in the `md` env (01-convert) to flat float64 arrays, sha256-pinned, then cluster in `hep`

traps.cause: the raw events file of Zenodo record v4 and earlier was never the one the features file describes (the record's 2022 note)
traps.fix: use record v5's events_anomalydetection_v2.h5
traps.symptom: matched 0 of 1.1 M rows under any permutation

traps.cause: the degree-9 tetrahedral quadrature scheme, not the solution, produces that number
traps.fix: use a quadrature degree that is exact for |∇e|² (degree 4 here); the P2 ladder uses degree 7, unaffected
traps.symptom: H1 error 2.319204e-06 for a quadratic that P3 represents exactly (1–2e-13 at quadrature degree 4)

traps.cause: createdb numbers the entries in a different order on each run, so a 1-in-50 subset by key picks different proteins on different boxes
traps.fix: choose the subset by name
traps.symptom: sha_db_lookup_by_key differs on all six runs

traps.cause: its self-alignment scores 8 bits, E = 85.6, far outside -e 10, and the prefilter passes nothing for it, with or without --comp-bias-corr 0
traps.cost: the first full run on each chip ($1.88) failed on Q156A1
traps.fix: search low-complexity proteins with --exhaustive-search 1 and a looser -e
traps.symptom: Q156A1 (ataxin-8, M followed by 79 Q) has no hit at all, not even itself

traps.cause: one HTTPS stream from EBI at about 1 MB/s for a 5.18 GB archive
traps.cost: about $0.36
traps.fix: fetch.py, run on AWS, with size and model-count checks
traps.symptom: the first fetch hit its TTL and spawn recorded no cost for it

traps.cause: the scans include the neck; bet without FSL's own robustfov crop mis-strips them, and drags FLIRT down too
traps.fix: run robustfov before bet (worst Dice 0.83 after, every one of the 125 improves)
traps.symptom: Plain `bet` on the whole-head image gives median Dice 0.75 and falls below 0.80 on 75 of 125 subjects (worst 0.34)

traps.cause: GNU nproc honours OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
traps.fix: read avg_cores (the measured parallelism), not nproc
traps.symptom: the `nproc` line in summary.txt reads 1 on a 16-vCPU box

traps.cause: GATK ships its PairHMM and SmithWaterman accelerators (Intel GKL) as x86-64 native libraries only; on AArch64 both fall back to Java, single-threaded, so --native-pair-hmm-threads is inert
traps.cost: 77 s at 1 thread vs 78 s at 8
traps.fix: do not buy cores for HaplotypeCaller on Graviton; buy the cheapest box that holds the heap and scatter intervals across tasks
traps.symptom: Unable to load libgkl_compression.so from native/libgkl_compression.so ... cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory (Possible cause: can't load AMD 64 .so on a AARCH64 platform)

traps.cause: the 91 entries holding an object over 50 MB run concurrently with 64 ordinary workers
traps.fix: run the big entries in a separate, narrower pool (6 workers)
traps.symptom: Putting the big entries first in a single 64-wide pool peaked at 54.8 GiB on the 64 GB box in a probe

traps.cause: transient errors streaming 672,176 objects from the public bucket
traps.cost: part of a first full Graviton4 run (six launches, $2.78 total)
traps.fix: `real.py` now retries
traps.symptom: two transient S3 errors (a 500 and a 503)

traps.blames: the claim that terra's integers are round(v × 10)
traps.cause: terra's intermediate dem * 10 is a float32 layer (FLT4S is terra's default type for temporary files); a product within half a float32 step of .5 becomes exactly .5 and std::round sends it up
traps.fix: keep the product in double, for example inside app() (that route was not run here); to reproduce terra, round(float32(v × 10))
traps.symptom: summing round(v × 10) computed in double misses terra's decimetre sums on 1,289 of 1,447 tracts, and the state total comes out 313,590 dm lower

traps.cause: for a geographic source GDAL 3.12.4 inserts a CENTER_LONG reprojection even for same-CRS, which disables GWKSumPreservingThread's exact rectangle-overlap path; the polygon path drops or splits quads on last-bit noise (last step inferred from code and loss pattern)
traps.fix: pass `-to INSERT_CENTER_LONG=FALSE` to gdalwarp -r sum when the target is the same CRS (exact on all three chips, 24-30% faster)
traps.symptom: gdalwarp -r sum on a lat/lon source loses 0.27% of the total (sum ratio 0.997324; 1,802,620 of 3,628,800 cells short by 0.5, 1.0 or 1.5 source pixels) on Intel and AMD; Graviton4 exact under defaults, fails under -et 0

traps.cause: where surface pressure is under 1000 hPa (45% of columns), GFS's 1000 hPa temperature and height are extrapolated; a property of the extrapolation, not of MetPy
traps.fix: mask to columns with surface pressure ≥ 1000 hPa; the mask is part of the claim
traps.symptom: hypsometric thickness disagrees with the file's Z500 − Z1000 by up to 4.43%, outside the recipe's 2% bound

traps.cause: thresh = 1e-20 with the default maxit = 1e5 stops the binomial path at λ 82 (gaussian at λ 91) and hands back a shorter path
traps.cost: a sizing run
traps.fix: control = list(maxit = 1e6); fail the run if a CV-selected λ falls below the certified path
traps.symptom: Convergence for 83th lambda value not reached … solutions for larger lambdas returned

traps.cause: the 16-vCPU Intel box is 8 cores x 2 hyperthreads, and this bandwidth-bound SCF gets nothing from the second thread
traps.fix: Size by cores, not vCPUs
traps.symptom: On Intel, ranks 9–16 buy nothing: 282.8 s at 8 ranks, 285.9 s at 16

traps.cause: a scaling study that resizes the instance at each rung is not measuring scaling: four ranks on a 16-vCPU box get the bandwidth of twelve idle cores (+17.9%)
traps.fix: Hold the box fixed, or report both
traps.symptom: 4 → 16 speedup 3.27× (81.7%) on right-sized boxes against 2.71× (67.8%) on the same box

traps.cause: chunked transfer with no Content-Length from UCI
traps.fix: fetch.py resumes with Range; completeness proved by an end-to-end gzip read (CRC-32 and length trailer) and the row count
traps.symptom: UCI serves the file chunked with no Content-Length and dropped the first fetch at 1.25 GB

traps.cause: the GDAC's daily files are rebuilt whenever a float's delayed-mode QC arrives; every 2023 file had been rewritten within the 30 days before staging
traps.fix: results from new bytes are a new measurement; the citable frozen copy is the SEANOE monthly snapshot doi:10.17882/42182
traps.symptom: stage-inputs.sh reports revised files when a reader re-stages, and fails unless REPIN=1

traps.cause: the climate env's x86 twin image has no `free` binary

traps.cause: spawn's stage-in moved 215 GB at the CLI default 143–187 MB/s

traps.symptom: stage-in took 19–25 minutes of a 22–28 minute bill; compute 2.9–3.9% of billed

traps.cause: bilby 1.0.4 scaled the PSD by the Tukey window's power loss; bilby 2.x does not

traps.symptom: every SNR x0.935 and the noise evidence x0.875 (-6376.32 against -7288.12) against a GWTC-2.1 release

traps.fix: read the walk tuner (walks_probe.py); raise maxmcmc, not naccept
traps.symptom: raising naccept 60 -> 120 changes nothing: 20.53M likelihood calls against 20.46M, same time

traps.cause: the release stores the reconstructed physical time; with time marginalisation geocent_time is the segment start, so the template shifts by 2 s
traps.fix: set geocent_time to the prior's fixed value, float(ifos.start_time)
traps.symptom: a published sample passed back to a time-marginalised likelihood returns ln L ≈ −1 instead of 323

traps.cause: lalsimulation changed three IMRPhenomXPHM defaults since 2.4.0: PrecVersion 223->300, FinalSpinMod 3->4, PhenomXHMReleaseVersion 122019->122022
traps.fix: gwreal.py sets the 2.4.0 values

traps.cause: the inpainted columns are a different map; Q and U differ on every pixel

traps.symptom: `I_STOKES_INP` differs from `I_STOKES` on all but 8 of 49,572,744 pixels (by up to 8.1 mK, against an rms of 0.11 mK)

traps.cause: truffle's static fallback price table has no Graviton coverage, so spawn cannot enforce the cost cap and correctly refuses rather than drop it
traps.fix: launch the rungs serially
traps.symptom: eight concurrent spawn task run calls throttled the AWS Price List API, and spawn refused to launch

traps.cause: the header's (of N) is a sum of autonormalisation weights, not a count
traps.fix: take HOMER's kept-target count from the GC-bin table in its log
traps.symptom: knownResults.txt header reads (of 44,221) for 44,217 sequences

traps.cause: HUMAnN 3.9 calls bowtie2-build with no --threads (bowtie2_build_opts=[], no flag to set it); its Python steps are serial too
traps.fix: none in HUMAnN 3.9; extra cores only shorten bowtie2 and diamond
traps.symptom: 38–46% of the wall time runs on one core; 16 vCPUs average 8–10 busy

traps.cause: the bioBakery server streams without a Content-Length

traps.symptom: the first 00-dbs run reported a failure after a complete, CRC-checked download

traps.cause: fasterq-dump --split-files gives both mates the same ID (@ERR2984773.1 …) and HUMAnN keys reads by the first word, merging the mates
traps.cost: measured on the 200k-pair canary: UNMAPPED 130,474 vs 228,931, RPK 377,084 vs 539,235

traps.symptom: Nothing fails: 30% less RPK, and 65.2% unaligned printed instead of 57.2%

traps.cause: HUMAnN 3.9 parses the last line of `metaphlan --version`, and MetaPhlAn 4.2.5 prints a database status line there; --bypass-prescreen also builds the index from all of ChocoPhlAn and ignores the profile

traps.symptom: HUMAnN 3.9's MetaPhlAn version check cannot pass against MetaPhlAn 4.2.5 without --bypass-prescreen

traps.cause: an unreferenced quantisation table (CAMELYON16's tables define 0 and 1, tiles use only 0), and on the 95 Radboud slides a table defined twice (a stripped overview image defines its own)
traps.fix: splice only the tables a tile references and does not define itself; jpegtran -copy none is accepted but re-codes the entropy data, so the rebuild would not be the TIFF's

traps.cause: at `-T 8` IQ-TREE 3.1.3's FreeRate fits vary run to run on one chip, so each run ends on its own tree

traps.cause: `-te` started from task 1's branch lengths, fitted under `Q.PFAM+I+R10` and 25–44% too long for LG+G4

traps.cause: kallisto estimates the fragment-length distribution from whichever pairs the 16 threads reach first

traps.cause: laspy parses the Classification Lookup VLR into names and keeps only [A-Za-z0-9 ] (laspy 2.7.0 vlrs/known.py)

traps.cause: fits UShER being executed twice under this image's snakemake 9.23 (not established)

traps.cause: the counting kernel is compiled for writable uint32 arrays; loky memory-maps any argument over 1 MB read-only, and the graph's indices cross 1 MB at 262,144 edges

traps.cause: under set -u an SSM-driven script has no $HOME

traps.cause: the 897x257 grid is not exactly mirror-symmetric: its wake line sits at y = 5.35e-8 and mirrored points miss their partners by up to 3.7e-5

traps.cause: upstream's test_vals residuals are the noise floor of a restart from a converged solution (RMS ρ ≈ 1e-12), i.e. the bits of the build that wrote them; test_vals and test_vals_aarch64 differ by up to 3.5e-5

traps.cause: a property of the aia.lev2_hc product's header, not of sunpy; the vector read as ecliptic of date is instead 0.249° off (about 17.7 years of precession)

traps.cause: gclib treats a gap of 4 bp or less as no intron (GFF_MIN_INTRON = 4, gff.h); Ensembl 116 has 57 such gaps

traps.cause: at -p 8 the record order and the STRG numbering follow which bundle finishes first
